# Results -- Study 329 (One-Month-Reversal) on the real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: each month, rank
S&P 500 names by **last month's** simple return; long the bottom quintile (last month's
*losers*), short the top quintile (last month's *winners*), hold one month, rebalance
(Jegadeesh 1990, Table I). Pinned against the microstructure-safe one-month-gap variant,
a random-portfolio control, a beta decomposition, and a sub-period split.
**Survivorship-biased**: the universe is the current S&P 500 projected backwards -- all
results are upper bounds. As-of **2026-06-15** (the panel is trimmed to the last complete
month, 2026-05-31; the in-progress June bar is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|------------------------|
| yfinance monthly (adj close), shared S&P 500 panel | 1990-01-31 -> 2026-05-31 | 437 months x 494 tickers | `fa033b6cedf6` |

Universe: ~398 stocks with a valid one-month signal in any given month; ~80 per quintile.

## skip=0 -- last month's rank (the Jegadeesh specification)

| Portfolio | Mean return | HAC *t* |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Loser quintile**  | **+24.73%/yr** | **+6.71** |
| Winner quintile     | +18.18%/yr     | +6.07     |
| **Spread (Loser - Winner)** | **+54.6 bps/mo = +6.55%/yr** | **+2.40** |
| Loser excess over equal-weight market | +5.51%/yr | +3.10 |

- The loser-winner **spread HAC *t* = +2.40** -- it *does* clear the inference bar of 2.0
  on the full sample. Hit-rate 52.0%. This is the canonical short-horizon reversal: last
  month's losers do beat last month's winners next month.
- But the spread is **not robust** (see the two killers below).

## The two killers

### 1. The bid-ask-bounce trap (skip=1, a one-month gap)

| Variant | Spread | HAC *t* |
|---------|--------|---------|
| skip=0 (last month's close forms *and* prices the trade) | +54.6 bps/mo | **+2.40** |
| **skip=1 (one-month gap before holding)** | **-4.9 bps/mo** | **-0.21** |

Inserting a single month between the formation close and the holding month annihilates the
effect (*t* falls from +2.40 to **-0.21**). A reversal that lives only when last month's
*close* both forms the signal and prices the entry is the textbook bid-ask-bounce illusion
(Jegadeesh 1990; Lehmann 1990; Lo-MacKinlay 1990): a stock that closed on the bid prints a
low return and "reverts" upward purely because the next print lands on the ask. The
tradable component, measured one month out, is gone.

### 2. Post-publication decay

| Period | Spread | HAC *t* | n months |
|--------|--------|---------|----------|
| 1990-2002 (pre/early publication) | +134.9 bps/mo | **+2.67** | 154 |
| 2003-2014 | +23.6 bps/mo | +1.07 | 144 |
| 2015-2026 | **-3.1 bps/mo** | **-0.10** | 137 |

The entire full-sample *t* is carried by the 1990s. Since ~2003 the spread is
indistinguishable from zero, and in the most recent decade it is slightly negative -- the
canonical McLean-Pontiff (2016) fade as decimalisation, electronic market-making and
statistical-arbitrage desks competed the liquidity rent away.

## Beta decomposition

| Leg | Beta vs equal-weight market | Alpha (ann) |
|-----|-----------------------------|-------------|
| Loser quintile | 1.290 | -- |
| Winner quintile | 0.977 | -- |
| **Spread (L-S, dollar-neutral)** | **0.313** | **+0.54%/yr** |

The dollar-neutral spread is nearly market-neutral (beta 0.31), so unlike Study 196's
long-only loser leg this is *not* simply disguised beta -- it is a real (if fragile)
cross-sectional anomaly. The problem is not beta; it is microstructure and decay.

## Tradability -- turnover and cost sweep

The loser quintile turns over **~78%** one-way each month (a one-month signal is, by
design, almost entirely refreshed every rebalance). Costs are counted one-way x NAV across
both legs, round-trip.

| One-way cost | Net spread | Net HAC *t* |
|--------------|------------|-------------|
| 0 bps  | +54.6 bps/mo | +2.40 |
| 5 bps  | +39.0 bps/mo | +1.72 |
| 10 bps | +23.3 bps/mo | +1.03 |
| 20 bps | -8.0 bps/mo  | -0.35 |

**Break-even one-way cost: ~17.4 bps.** Even at an optimistic 10 bps the net *t* drops
below 1; at a realistic all-in 20 bps the strategy is loss-making. Combined with the
skip=1 collapse, the gross spread is a measurement artefact long before it is a trade.

## Random-portfolio null

A random quintile of the same size, drawn 100x per month, has mean excess over the market
of **-1.4 bps** -- centred at zero, confirming the loser excess (when it exists) is signal,
not concentration.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds reversal when it exists

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`, n_firms=150, n_months=250)
the same quintile engine recovers a spread monotone in the planted one-month reversal and
near zero on the null:

| Planted reversal | Spread mean/mo | Spread *t* |
|------------------|----------------|------------|
| 0.00 (null)      | ~+0.2%         | ~0-2 (by chance) |
| +0.05            | ~+14%          | ~+90-130 |
| -0.05 (momentum) | negative       | strongly < 0 |

The engine is a faithful detector; the real-tape verdict is about the market, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- MIXED.** Real on the raw full-sample tape (spread HAC *t* = +2.40, clears
  the bar) **and dollar-neutral, not beta** (spread beta 0.31, alpha +0.54%/yr) -- but
  **None once you defuse bid-ask bounce** (skip=1 *t* = -0.21) **or look past 2002**
  (2015-2026 *t* = -0.10). The certified component is the 1990s liquidity rent; the modern,
  microstructure-clean component is indistinguishable from zero. Survivorship-biased upper
  bound throughout.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** ~78% monthly one-way turnover; break-even ~17 bps; net *t* < 1
  by 10 bps and negative by 20 bps. A 100%-refreshed monthly book of a signal that already
  evaporates one month out cannot be traded.
- **Is it bid-ask bounce? -- CONFIRMED.** The one-month gap removes the entire effect.
